hypotheses.justification: The statement holds for every real sequence N. Write E n for the energy sum and B n = 2·(crossing sum) + 2·(rank-decrease sum). These are real numbers with 0 ≤ E n (a sum of squares) and E n ≤ B n. The bound E n ≤ B n is the private lemma `sum_partitionVertexMidrank_permutation_energy_le` (line 7785), which takes no hypothesis on N. Then |E n / N n| = E n / |N n| ≤ B n / |N n| = |B n / N n|. This uses `abs_div` and dividing an inequality by the nonnegative number |N n|. The case N n = 0 is covered by the junk value x / 0 = 0: both sides are 0. Also B n / N n = 2·(cross/N n) + 2·(rank/N n), and this tends to 0 by `hcross` and `hrank`, exactly as in the existing `hlimit` step. So `squeeze_zero_norm'` (or `squeeze_zero'` applied to the absolute values) gives that E n / N n tends to 0. Only the existing `hnonnegative` and `hupper` steps use `hN`; they are replaced by this absolute-value bound. Negative values of N are no problem either: E/N and B/N then both lie in [B/N, 0].
